source.title: The BUTTER Zone: An Empirical Study of Training Dynamics in Fully Connected Neural Networks
source.authors: C. Tripp; J. Perr-Sauer; Lucas Hayne; Monte Lunacek; Jamil Gafur

record.tranche_reason: The study empirically sweeps MLP size, batch size, optimizer, and L1/L2 regularization, using test performance and training trajectories to examine generalization; it does not reproduce the specific model and dataset settings in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports aggregate sweep findings and figure descriptions. It does not report fixed random-label fit versus natural-label test performance, convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Values used only to construct plotted curves are not separately extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own results on performance beyond interpolation and adaptive-versus-SGD generalization in a broader set of fully connected ReLU networks and tasks, including MNIST.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors primarily present an empirical dataset and preliminary patterns: larger networks achieve lower minimum test losses beyond interpolation, batch size mainly affects training efficiency, and optimizer choice moderately affects performance without changing the overall dynamics. They emphasize that the analysis is empirical and requires further validation.
record.recipe_differences: Large empirical sweeps of fully connected MLPs on 13 tabular learning tasks, rather than the specific image and language benchmark settings in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Parameter count, depth, batch size, learning rate, L1/L2 regularization, optimizer, task, and network shape affect reported performance patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches require more epochs to minimize test loss, while their effect on minimum test loss is described as weak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size changes training speed and sample efficiency in fully connected networks.

fits_no_version.finding: L1/L2 regularization can delay or reduce overtraining, while heavy penalties can increase unpenalized test loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L1/L2 penalties trade off delayed overtraining against poorer best held-out performance in some MLP settings.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, August 2023
record.problems: The paper calls its analysis preliminary and empirical. Reported outcomes are largely aggregate qualitative descriptions of figures; exact per-condition values and uncertainty estimates are not given in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately described numeric outcomes were available in the text; plotted curves and individual task-level values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: No near-complete fixed random-label fitting and corresponding chance-level held-out comparison; partial label noise does not establish this.
The original one-hidden-layer, width-only, converged classification-error comparison is not reproduced; no downsampled CIFAR-10 experiment is reported.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or learned local-connectivity experiment.
No language benchmarks, systematic broader-tuning comparison, decoupled weight decay, or Adam-to-SGD switching experiment; training-performance parity is not established in the reported comparison.

No stated held-out penalty at a common epoch budget or workload-dependent batch threshold; longer-training recovery, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, and regularization adaptations are not evaluated as remedies.
No dropout experiment or dropout interaction with training-set size, augmentation, or weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Minimum test losses are selected using the held-out trajectory; they should not be interpreted as final-epoch results or performance on a separate untouched evaluation set. Weak evidence for epoch-wise double descent does not challenge V2, which concerns width beyond interpolation.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random-label versus natural-label training and held-out comparison.
The study sweeps MLP parameter count and reports performance beyond the interpolation threshold, but does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 as specified.
No convolutional networks or fully connected versus convolutional comparison.
Tests Adam, SGD, and RMSProp on rectangular MLPs, not the image and language benchmarks or the broader tuning and recovery conditions listed.
Batch size is swept, but the paper does not compare a stated fixed-epoch generalization gap against a workload-dependent threshold or test the listed recipe adaptations.
Tests L1 and L2 regularization, but not dropout or dropout interactions with data augmentation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal and retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: FC MLPs in the Primary Sweep
rows.size_stated: 20 different numbers of trainable parameters; 25–25 in Table II
rows.operation_detail: Swept parameter count and assessed test performance across tasks and topologies.
rows.measure: Median minimum test loss; generalization performance
rows.value: Larger networks perform better, even well beyond the interpolation threshold; both effects have diminishing returns.
rows.locator: Section IV-A, Primary Sweep discussion; Figure 1
rows.note: The finding is stated across the sweep; no per-task numeric values are given in the text.
rows.check: The parameter range is 2^5–2^25, not 25–25. The outcome is median minimum test loss within 3000 epochs, rather than classification error after verified convergence. Parameter count varies across depths and shapes, so this is broader than a controlled width-only comparison.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V2 as written. Larger networks achieve lower median minimum test loss beyond interpolation within 3000 epochs; corresponding classification-error trends after training to convergence are not established.
source_check.locator_found: Section IV-A, pp. 4–5; Figure 1 caption; Appendix A, p. 12.
source_check.problem: The reported loss trend does not establish V2's classification-error trend under training to convergence.

rows.subject: FC MLPs in the Batch Size Sweep
rows.operation_detail: Swept batch size and assessed test performance and epochs to minimum test loss.
rows.measure: Test loss and epochs to minimize test loss
rows.value: Batch size has a weak effect on generalization performance; larger batches can increase the epochs to minimize test loss. The butter-zone tends to shift upwards as batch size increases.
rows.note: The paper describes a weak generalization effect and an upward shift in the plotted low-loss region; it does not state numeric losses or compare fixed-epoch outcomes explicitly.
rows.check: Minimum test loss and epochs to reach it do not establish worse held-out performance at a common epoch budget. The upward shift describes the epoch axis, not an increase in minimum loss; the text gives no direction for its weak generalization effect.

rows.subject: FC MLPs in the Optimizer Sweep: Adam, SGD, and RMSProp
rows.size_stated: rectangular networks from the Primary Sweep
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizers at several batch sizes and learning rates.
rows.measure: Training speed and quality; median test loss
rows.value: RMSProp and SGD both perform similarly to Adam in these experiments; optimizer choice moderately impacts training speed and quality but does not result in wholly different dynamics.
rows.note: The reported comparison does not show adaptive Adam generalizing worse than SGD in this setting.
rows.check: The similarity statement is supported by Figure 27. Specify that this figure uses learning rate 0.01 for SGD versus 0.001 for the adaptive optimizers. The sweep includes momentum variants and MNIST; it is not exclusively non-image tabular tasks. No numeric optimizer gap is stated.

rows.subject: Rectangular FC MLPs in the Regularization Sweep
rows.operation_detail: Applied a sweep of L1 and L2 kernel regularization strengths.
rows.measure: Unpenalized test loss and overtraining behavior
rows.value: Heavy regularization can increase test losses; it can also delay the onset and severity of overtraining. Regularization did not induce deep double descent in these experiments.
rows.note: This reports L1/L2 effects, not the dropout effect specified by V6.
rows.check: L1/L2 penalties do not test dropout. Figure 6 explicitly uses unpenalized test loss, while Figure 23 warns that its displayed losses include regularization penalties; these measures should not be conflated.
